title: upgrade: attention kernels -> FlashAttentionV2 with fused ops, rotary/rope improvements, KV-batching scheduling
author: Sanjay Patel
description:
Motivation: Upgrade the runtime attention kernels to a maintained FlashAttentionV2 implementation with fused operations and improved rotary/rope support, plus scheduler changes to enable KV-aware continuous batching. This PR targets long-sequence and high-concurrency workloads where per-token cost and tail latency are critical. Summary of changes:

- Integrates FlashAttentionV2 core kernels (C++/CUDA) with a thin runtime adapter.
- Adds fused QKV->attn fused ops to reduce kernel launches and intermediate memory.
- Improves rotary/rope application paths to avoid extra copies for long-sequence inference.
- Adds KV-batching-aware scheduling heuristics and a fast path when KV cache hits are common.
- KV cache refactor: reduces per-request allocation and adds a small object pool to avoid allocator churn.
- Backwards compatible runtime switch: runtime.config.runtime.attn.preferred_impl = [auto|flashv2|fallback].

Performance: Internal microbenchmarks (A100, seq=4096, batch=8, 8-bit quantized) show throughput increases of 15-28% vs current kernels and median p95 latency reduction of 10-22% on long-history workloads. Memory peak decreased ~12% in our bench suite due to fused ops and reduced temporaries. See docs/benchmarks/attn_upgrade.md for detailed numbers and run commands.

Checklist:
- [x] Core kernels integrated and compiled in CI with CUDA 12 toolchain.
- [x] Scheduler heuristics implemented and covered by unit tests.
- [x] KV cache regressions tested against replay harness.
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime config; safe fallback enabled.
- [x] Docs and internal runbooks added.

Notes & follow-ups:
- A small subset of older GPUs (sm_70) will use the fallback path until we backport a kernel variant. Tracked in ENG-10012.
- We observed a flaky bench related to memory reclamation on CI; fixed by a small allocator guard in this PR.

Related: PRs updating Python SDK examples and docs will follow to expose the runtime flag and benchmark recipes.

Hannah Kim: I saw a minor race in KV pool teardown in integration runs. Please ensure shutdown ordering. (requested changes)

release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV ops, improved rotary/rope paths, KV-aware continuous batching and scheduler heuristics. Expected throughput improvements (15-28%) and reduced memory usage. Feature is behind runtime.config.runtime.attn.preferred_impl and falls back on unsupported hardware.
notes_for_release: Enable runtime.config.runtime.attn.preferred_impl=flashv2 in canary to validate on production traffic.
Monitor attn.kernel.invoke_time and kv_cache.hit_rate for regressions.
Rollout plan: canary -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with automatic rollback on error budget.
